pages.alt: Mira, Tavi and Sol stand beside the little wall door, its ramp and the finished map from their first adventure.

pages.text:
Mira had just put the first adventure’s map away.

CHIME! The little wall door opened. The same blue-and-gold parcel rolled down the ramp.
pages.subtext: Mira, Sol and Tavi had seen this parcel at the end of their last adventure.
pages.alt: Mira, Sol and Tavi watch the same blue-and-gold parcel roll down the ramp into the library.

pages.text:
Mira untied the ribbon. The parcel opened, and a round Moon Lantern rose from inside.

A card said: TAKE THE MOON LANTERN TO THE BALCONY BEFORE THE FIRST EVENING STAR.
pages.subtext: The card showed the lantern and the balcony at the top of the star room.
pages.alt: The open parcel holds the Moon Lantern. A card shows the lantern and the balcony.

pages.text:
The friends carried the lantern to the workshop, but it was too wide for the door.

Pax came out. “Hello! I’m Pax. I help things fit together. I can help you carry the lantern.”
pages.subtext: Pax is the new friend in this adventure.
pages.alt: Pax greets Mira, Sol and Tavi beside the workshop door. The lantern is wider than the doorway.

pages.text:
Pax rolled out a round tray and placed the lantern inside. It fit exactly.

Three lantern pictures lit up beside the door.
pages.subtext: The door will open when the team chooses the whole lantern.
pages.alt: The lantern fits inside a round tray. Three big lantern pictures glow beside the door.

pages.badge: TRY IT · WHICH HAS EVERY PART?
pages.text:
Look at all three lantern pictures.

One has every part. One has a gap. One has an extra shape.

Point to the lantern with every part, no gap and no extra shape.
pages.subtext: Choose before you turn the page.
pages.alt: The first lantern has a gap. The second is round with every part. The third has an extra triangle attached.

pages.text:
WHOLE LANTERN.
NO GAP. NO EXTRA.

“This is the whole lantern,” said Pax. “Every part of this lantern is here.”
pages.subtext: Whole means all of the lantern is here. No part is missing. No extra part has been added. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The round Moon Lantern fills its tray and is labelled whole, with no gap and no extra shape.

pages.text:
The gold seal clicked open. Behind it was a short bridge made from four glowing floor tiles.

Words lit beside the first tile: VISIT EVERY LIGHT ONCE.
pages.subtext: Mira pointed from START to FINISH. All four lights were easy to see.
pages.alt: Four glowing floor tiles make a short bridge from START to FINISH.

pages.text:
Point to the glowing tiles from START to FINISH.

Touch every tile once. Skip none. Touch none twice.
pages.subtext: Keep your finger moving along one clear route.
pages.alt: Four large separate glowing tiles wait in one row for the child to point to each tile once.

pages.text:
ONE · TWO · THREE · FOUR.

Every light was touched once. None was skipped. None was touched twice.
pages.subtext: To count these lights, touch each light once. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The same four tiles show one numbered footprint each, with no empty tile and no tile carrying two footprints.

pages.text:
Sol bounced across: “One, two, three, three, four!”

The bridge flashed red instead of opening. What was different about Sol’s path?
pages.subtext: Look closely at the footprints on every tile before you turn.
pages.alt: The four-tile bridge shows one footprint on tiles one, two and four, but two footprints on tile three.

pages.text:
TILE THREE WAS TOUCHED TWICE.

“The footprints show us what happened,” said Tavi.
pages.subtext: Sol tried again and touched every tile once. The bridge opened. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: One picture shows two footprints on tile three. A second picture shows one footprint on every tile.

pages.text:
The bridge led to another narrow door. Beside it was a tray with four empty spaces.

“The lantern is still too wide,” said Pax. “We can carry it in pieces and put it back together.”
pages.subtext: Three pictures showed three ways to split the lantern into pieces.
pages.alt: Three pictures beside the narrow door show different ways to split the lantern into pieces.

pages.text:
Which picture passes all three checks?

1. It fills the whole circle.
2. Its pieces do not cover each other.
3. Its pieces are the same size.
pages.subtext: Point to one picture before you turn.
pages.alt: One picture has a gap. In one, pieces cover each other. One fills the circle with four same-size pieces.

pages.text:
Trace around the circle. Is it full?

Trace the lines between the pieces. Do any pieces cover each other?

Look at their sizes. Are they the same?
pages.subtext: Check every question before you choose.
pages.alt: The three choices stay visible while the child checks the outside edge, the lines between pieces and the piece sizes.

pages.text:
WHOLE CIRCLE FILLED.
NO PIECES COVER EACH OTHER.
PIECES THE SAME SIZE.

The door opened.
pages.subtext: This picture passed all three checks. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: Four same-size pieces fill the chosen circle without covering each other.

pages.text:
Pax touched the picture. CLICK! The lantern split along the same lines.

Its four pieces dropped into four spaces on the tray. Now they could fit through the narrow door.
pages.subtext: All four pieces are easy to see on the tray.
pages.alt: Four same-size lantern pieces sit in four spaces on a tray.

pages.text:
Move every lantern piece from the tray into the round outline.

Use every piece once. Leave none behind.
pages.subtext: Which edges fit together? Try before you turn.
pages.alt: Four recognisable coloured lantern pieces wait beside a matching empty round outline for reassembly.

pages.text:
FOUR PARTS FIT.
THE MOON LANTERN IS WHOLE AGAIN.

Mira looked at the tray. All four spaces were empty because every piece was back in the lantern.
pages.subtext: Every lantern piece was used once. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The round Moon Lantern is whole again and all four tray spaces are empty.

pages.text:
The next door opened into a room with a long table. Two pairs of pieces lay on it.

Which pair has two pieces that are the same size: Pair A or Pair B?
pages.subtext: Look at both pieces in each pair before you turn.
pages.alt: Pair A has two pieces of the same size. Pair B has one big piece and one small piece.

pages.text:
PAIR A: EQUAL IN SIZE.
PAIR B: NOT EQUAL IN SIZE.

“Both pieces in Pair A are the same size,” said Pax. “They are equal in size.”
pages.subtext: One piece in Pair B is bigger than the other.
pages.alt: Pair A is equal in size. Pair B has one big piece and one small piece.

pages.text:
At the next door, Sol began to put the lantern together. He filled three of its four spaces.

“Is the lantern whole now?” he asked.
pages.subtext: Look at all four spaces. Decide before you turn.
pages.alt: The lantern has four spaces. Three have pieces in them. One space is empty.

pages.text:
ONE SPACE IS EMPTY.
THE LANTERN IS NOT WHOLE YET.

“We still need one more piece,” said Mira.
pages.subtext: The team put in the fourth piece. Now all four spaces were filled.
pages.alt: The fourth piece fills the empty space. The lantern is whole again.

pages.text:
RATTLE! A triangle rolled beside the whole lantern.

“The lantern is whole,” said Tavi. “This triangle is here too, but it does not fit anywhere.”
pages.subtext: The triangle is extra. It is not part of the lantern. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: The whole lantern is inside its round shape. An extra triangle sits outside.

pages.text:
Pax lifted some pieces from the lantern tray.

How many pieces is Pax holding?
How many pieces make the whole lantern?
pages.subtext: Look at Pax’s hands and the whole tray. Say both numbers before you turn.
pages.alt: Pax holds two pieces while all four lantern spaces stay visible.

pages.text:
TWO PIECES HELD.
FOUR PIECES MAKE THE WHOLE LANTERN.

“Both answers matter,” said Pax. “I am holding two. The whole lantern has four.”
pages.subtext: Say both numbers again. Find the optional code.
pages.alt: Labels show the two pieces Pax holds and the four spaces in the whole lantern.

pages.text:
Before the friends put the lantern together one last time, Tavi asked, “What happened when Sol first crossed the bridge?”

A. He missed one tile.
B. He touched one tile twice.
C. He touched every tile once.
pages.subtext: Think back to Sol’s footprints. Pax waits without giving the answer.
pages.alt: Tavi presents three picture choices: an untouched tile, a tile with two footprints, and a row with one footprint per tile.

pages.text:
SOL TOUCHED ONE TILE TWICE.

The friends kept a picture of his first try so they could see what changed. Then Sol crossed again and touched every tile once.
pages.subtext: The two pictures show the first try and the new try side by side.
pages.alt: Sol's first path with two footprints on one tile and his new path with one footprint per tile are shown side by side.

pages.text:
Every lantern piece went back into its place.

The Moon Lantern was whole again. Together, the friends carried it through the last door and onto the balcony.
pages.subtext: Before they left, they checked that every piece was in the lantern. The tray was empty.
pages.alt: Mira, Tavi, Sol and Pax carry the whole glowing Moon Lantern onto the balcony.

pages.text:
1. CHECK THE WHOLE: no gap and no extra piece.
2. CHECK THE COUNT: touch each thing once.
3. CHECK THE PIECES: fill the whole, keep them apart and compare their sizes.
pages.subtext: Can you find a page that shows each check?
pages.alt: Pax shows three picture cards: a whole shape, one footprint on each tile and pieces of the same size.

pages.text:
The lantern lit up as the first evening star appeared.

Two colours began to repeat across its round face: blue, gold, blue, gold.
pages.subtext: Next: Book E03 · The Fold Makes a Pattern
pages.alt: The whole Moon Lantern glows beneath one evening star while blue and gold repeat across its round face.
